about: Every number this video shows or says, with its source. Trades-first bank lesson 3 ('Raise your prices; most trades already did', research/runs/2026-10-28-trades-insights.md); replaces the old price-raise lesson (Kahneman, Knetsch, Thaler 1986, a non-trade study). Every page below re-read with WebFetch on Oct 28, 2026 (America/Chicago), and only what each page says is used.

jobber.title: Blue Collar Strong: The 2026 Home Service Trends Report
jobber.published: page modified Mar 25, 2026 (no original date on the page)
jobber.method: survey of 1,050 US home service business owners, conducted through Conjointly in December 2025; margin of error plus or minus 3 points at 90% confidence
jobber.cleaningQuote: only 55% reporting an increase (the lowest of any trade on the page)
jobber.reasonsQuote: Inflation (72%) and labor costs (50%) are the most common reasons; the chart labels the 72% 'inflation and material costs'
jobber.scope: Shares are of the surveyed owners in each trade (HVAC 83% = HVAC businesses in the survey). 'Last year' is the page's word: the survey ran in December 2025. The page gives no size of the increases, no customer reaction and no plans for next year: none are said. Jobber sells field service software: said 'Jobber sells software'. Voice says 'inflation' for the 72% (the page's text), the chart's 'material costs' wording is not relied on.

bls.title: Employment Cost Index, June 2026 (news release USDL-26-1270)
bls.repairRow: Installation, maintenance, and repair (Table 8, civilian workers, wages and salaries, 12-month percent change, June 2026, not seasonally adjusted)
bls.allRow: All workers, civilian, wages and salaries, 12 months ending June 2026
bls.constructionRow: Construction, extraction, farming, fishing, and forestry occupations (Table 8); context for the caption only, not said (the group includes farming, fishing and forestry)
bls.scope: Said 'pay for install and repair workers rose three point seven percent in the year to June; all workers, three point two'. Wages and salaries only (not benefits).

note.source: OURS: the letter is advice, the bank's takeaway reworded without a number (no rate is recommended)
note.line1: Starting the first of next month, our rates go up.
note.line2: Our labor and material costs rose this year.
note.line3: Anything you've already approved stays at the price we quoted.
